annotations.title: The figure.
annotations.text: To be the figure of his ſubſtance, ſignifieth nothing els but that vvhich S. Paul ſpeaketh in other vvordes to the Philippians c. 2. v. 6. that he is the forme and moſt expreſſe reſemblance of his fathers ſubſtance. So S. Ambroſe and others expound it, and the Greeke vvord [1] Character is very ſignificant to that purpoſe. [2] Note alſo by this place, that the Sonne, though he be a figure of his Fathers ſubſtance, is notvvithſtanding of the ſame ſubſtance. So Chriſtes body in the Sacrament and his myſtical death and ſacrifice in the ſame, though called a figure, image, or repreſentation of Chriſtes viſible body and ſacrifice vpon the Croſſe, yet may be and is the ſelf ſame in ſubſtance.

notes.text: The B. Sacrament a figure and yet the true body.

annotations.title: Let al the Angels adore.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> The Heretikes maruel that vve adore Chriſt in the B. Sacrament, vvhen they might learne by this place, that vvhereſoeuer his perſon is, there it ought to be adored both of men and Angels. And vvhere they ſay it vvas not made preſent in the Sacrament nor inſtituted to be adored, vve anſvver that no more vvas he incarnate purpoſely to be adored: but yet ſtraight vpon his deſcending from heauen, it vvas the duety both of Angels and al other creatures to adore him.

notes.text: The adoration of Christ in the B. Sacrament.
